item.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
item.description: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.

item.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
item.description: The proposed Character.ai bankruptcy sale includes sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors, the state AGs said.

item.title: AI data centers are becoming harder to build, and neoclouds are feeling it
item.description: ⁠Nvidia has made clear⁠ it won’t backstop an AI data center until it’s nearly ready to run, and that’s landing just as neoclouds report construction delays and more expensive debt. The message to developers is that land, power, and a finished building matter more than a pitch deck. ⁠Anita Verma-Lallian⁠ has been selling exactly that. […]

item.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse
item.description: Amazon and Meta are discussing a potential deal that would end a two-month-long blockade of Muse.

item.title: The questions Jensen Huang and Nvidia will still have to answer about Megaspeed
item.description: The central question for investigators is what Nvidia knew about where those chips ended up and whether Huang's affair with a Megaspeed executive gave the company reason to doubt Megaspeed's assurances.

item.title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to US industrial might — not a champion
item.description: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that what the market cheered Monday, Jensen Huang's White House–backed return as Nvidia's CEO and board member, could prove a giant mistake, exposing the directors to "historic" personal liability from a growing pile of lawsuits and raising the question of whether the country is celebrating a company that has helped put advanced chips in its adversaries' hands.

item.title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy
item.description: It's a remarkable stance for a company that spent the last two weeks finding out what happens without its founder.

item.title: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
item.description: The Nvidia founder apologized to his staff on Tuesday and said he was grateful for a second chance to lead the company.

item.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
item.description: As millions embrace personal AI assistants, a new benchmark reveals that even the most advanced AI models struggle to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely without introducing potential new problems.

item.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
item.description: Walmart now lets customers shop Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.

item.title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself
item.description: The startup's encrypted AI architecture is designed to prevent even the company itself from accessing users' private data.
